questions.stem: An ionic bond is formed when

options.text: two atoms share a pair of electrons equally
electrons are completely transferred from one atom to another
both electrons of a shared pair come from the same atom
positive ions are surrounded by a sea of delocalised electrons

questions.explanation: In ionic bonding a metal atom loses one or more electrons to a non-metal atom. The resulting oppositely charged ions are then held together by strong electrostatic attraction, which is the ionic bond itself.

distractorRationale.a: Equal sharing describes a non-polar covalent bond
distractorRationale.c: That describes a dative or co-ordinate covalent bond
distractorRationale.d: That describes metallic bonding

questions.stem: How many pairs of electrons are shared between the two nitrogen atoms in a nitrogen molecule, N2?
questions.explanation: A nitrogen atom has five outer electrons and needs three more to reach an octet. Each atom therefore contributes three electrons to sharing, making three shared pairs, that is a triple bond. The strength of that triple bond explains why nitrogen gas is so unreactive.

distractorRationale.a: One shared pair would leave each nitrogen with only six outer electrons
distractorRationale.b: Two shared pairs is the double bond found in oxygen, which has six outer electrons
distractorRationale.d: Nitrogen has only five outer electrons, so it cannot share four pairs

questions.stem: A solid does not conduct electricity but its molten form does. It has a high melting point and dissolves readily in water. The solid is most likely
questions.explanation: Only ionic solids show this exact combination. The ions are locked in the lattice in the solid state so no current flows, but melting frees them to carry charge. Strong electrostatic attraction throughout the lattice accounts for the high melting point, and polar water molecules pull the ions apart on dissolving.

distractorRationale.a: Simple molecular solids have low melting points and never conduct, molten or otherwise
distractorRationale.c: A metal conducts in the solid state because its delocalised electrons are already mobile
distractorRationale.d: Giant covalent solids such as diamond and silicon(IV) oxide are insoluble in water and do not conduct when molten

questions.stem: Element P has atomic number 20 and element Q has atomic number 17. The formula of the compound formed between P and Q is
questions.explanation: P has configuration 2, 8, 8, 2 so it loses two electrons to form P2+. Q has configuration 2, 8, 7 so it gains one electron to form Q-. Two Q- ions are needed to balance one P2+, giving PQ2. This is calcium chloride, CaCl2.

distractorRationale.a: PQ would leave the total charge at +1 rather than zero
distractorRationale.c: This reverses the charges, treating P as forming a 1+ ion and Q a 2- ion
distractorRationale.d: This is the pattern for a 3+ metal with a 2- non-metal, which does not apply here

questions.stem: The bond formed between the nitrogen atom of ammonia and a hydrogen ion to give the ammonium ion, NH4+, is described as
questions.explanation: A hydrogen ion has no electrons at all, so it cannot contribute one to a shared pair. The nitrogen atom of ammonia supplies both electrons of its lone pair. A shared pair in which both electrons come from the same atom is a dative or co-ordinate covalent bond.

distractorRationale.a: No electrons are transferred; the pair is shared between nitrogen and hydrogen
distractorRationale.b: There are no delocalised electrons or metal atoms involved
distractorRationale.d: Hydrogen bonding is a weak attraction between molecules, not a bond within an ion

questions.stem: Graphite conducts electricity while diamond does not, although both are made only of carbon. This is because in graphite

options.text: the carbon atoms are held by ionic bonds
each carbon uses only three of its four outer electrons in bonding, leaving one delocalised
the carbon atoms are free to move through the structure

questions.explanation: In graphite each carbon forms three covalent bonds within a flat hexagonal layer, so the fourth outer electron is not tied to any one atom. These delocalised electrons move freely along the layers and carry current. In diamond all four outer electrons are used in bonds, leaving none free.

distractorRationale.a: Graphite is entirely covalent; there are no ions in it
distractorRationale.c: The carbon atoms themselves stay fixed; it is the electrons that move
distractorRationale.d: Graphite contains no ions, so ionic conduction is impossible

questions.stem: Carbon dioxide has a low sublimation point because the covalent bonds between carbon and oxygen are weak.
questions.explanation: False. The C=O double bonds inside each molecule are very strong and are not broken when solid carbon dioxide sublimes. What is overcome are the weak van der Waals forces between separate CO2 molecules, and these require very little energy.

options.text: Sharing of electron pairs between atoms
Transfer of electrons from one atom to another

distractorRationale.c: Covalent bonds are formed by sharing electrons, which is different from ionic bonding.
distractorRationale.d: Ionic bonds usually occur between metals and non-metals, not between two non-metals.
